A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey and contain readable main text, figures, tables, references, and appendices. Retained, relocated, and added material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 presents a literature taxonomy and descriptive benchmark catalogues. Reported model outcomes are attributed to cited studies; no original empirical study is reported.

after.justification: Appendix D and Table 2 introduce the authors' quantitative analysis of corpus reuse across surveyed benchmarks, qualifying as original data-analysis results. The performance comparisons in Table 4 remain attributed to earlier studies.

M1.justification: The four-category taxonomy and its subcategories are retained. Neither version proposes a model or training algorithm; the expanded explanation in Section 2 clarifies existing multiple-category assignments.

E1.justification: No new datasets or tasks are used for model training or evaluation. Game-Time is added to the literature taxonomy, while the new corpus analyses concern resources already surveyed.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed model against baselines. V3 Table 4 compiles published comparisons between end-to-end and cascaded systems, without introducing comparator evaluations conducted by this work.

E3.justification: No benchmark evaluation procedures, splits, budgets, or model settings are revised. Tables 5–6 and Appendix I newly describe existing metrics; the additional survey tabulations do not establish changes to benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: Appendices D, E, and H add systematic analyses of corpus reuse, real versus synthetic audio usage, and published end-to-end versus cascaded-system outcomes. These substantially extend the supplementary analysis beyond v1's taxonomy and modality catalogues.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures. Table 2 adds descriptive counts; Table 4's use of 'significantly' supplies no new uncertainty estimation or significance test.

E6.justification: V3 adds corpus-use counts, including AudioSet and Common Voice at eight benchmarks each and LibriSpeech at seven, plus Table 3's audio-source classifications. Table 4 adds literature-derived outcome summaries, including cascaded advantages on VoiceBench/VoxEval and an end-to-end advantage on SALMon. These are newly reported survey results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Neither version contains formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The added taxonomy examples and metric explanations introduce no formal mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: an evaluation-focused LALM survey, a four-category taxonomy, and identification of challenges and future directions.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds task-dependent explanations for cascaded systems' strengths on semantic tasks and end-to-end models' strengths on nuanced auditory perception. Appendix E explains reasons for synthetic-audio use. The main challenges and stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Tables 3, 5, and 6 add audio-provenance and benchmark-metric details, supplemented by Appendix I. However, v1's direct survey-collection repository link is removed, although the promise to release and maintain the collection remains.

R1.justification: V3 adds Game-Time to Figure 3 and references for Game-Time, the original Story Cloze task, UTMOS, and BERTScore. Existing references and the central novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: Section 2 expands a brief overlap footnote into an explanatory paragraph with examples. Appendices gain subsections and updated cross-references, alongside light prose edits and acknowledgments. The main narrative and section order remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Five new tables display corpus reuse, audio provenance, comparative outcomes, and benchmark features/metrics. Original modality Tables 2–5 are retained as Tables 7–10, and Figure 3 adds Game-Time. New Table 2 has a minor highlighting inconsistency: Clotho's five uses are bold despite the caption specifying more than five.

improvement.justification: V3 makes benchmark selection easier through structured feature, metric, and provenance tables, while adding useful task-dependent comparison guidance and quantitative support for existing corpus-reuse concerns. These incremental gains improve the retained survey and outweigh the removed collection link and minor Table 2 highlighting error.
